manifest.name: dsh-weixin
manifest.description: DSH ecosystem channel plugin: WeChat (personal) for DeepSeek Harness — native iLink Bot API, QR login, per-chat resident Agents, full media exchange. No OpenClaw gateway, no forwarding.

bundle.text:
# The dsh-weixin bundle patch: resident personal-WeChat channel over dsh-base.
# No Host, HTTP server, or browser plugin — a headless daemon profile whose
# only surface is your WeChat account via the official iLink Bot API
# (same protocol behind the Tencent-maintained openclaw-weixin plugin).
#
# This bundle is environment-agnostic. Credentials live under
# stateDir (default ~/.dsh/weixin-channel/state), scoped by OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR
# so they never touch any OpenClaw installation's state.

- id: system-prompt
  config:
    persona: >-
      You are a helpful assistant living in WeChat instant messaging,
      powered by the {{model}} model. Your working directory is {{cwd}}. Keep
      replies concise and IM-friendly by default; use short paragraphs instead
      of huge walls of text; expand into detail only when asked.

      Media handling: users may send images, voice, video, or files; each is
      saved to a local path included in the message — view or read it with
      your tools before replying. To deliver a local file back to the user,
      emit a line exactly like [[wxfile:/absolute/path/to/file]] (optionally
      with surrounding explanation text). Images, videos, and generic
      attachments are all supported; use it whenever a file serves the user
      better than prose.

# The shared module-reload HMR row stays off; the launcher's watch-only
# fallback still keeps the user patch layers live until the run exits.
- id: hmr
  disabled: true

- id: tools
  config:
    # Keep the same temporary process-wide Code Mode opt-in as the Web surface.
    mode: !!js process.env.DSH_TOOLS_MODE

- insert:
    # Code Mode is a core execution capability, not a Web component.
    - id: code-runtime
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-code-runtime-worker-thread'

    # The WeChat channel bridge: QR login on first boot (the QR link is
    # written to loginQrFile and logged), then a getUpdates long-poll loop
    # driving one resident Agent per chat peer, replying via sendMessage.
    - id: weixin-bridge
      name: 'dsh-weixin'

readme.text:
> Part of the **DSH ecosystem** — channel plugins built on the [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://npm.im/@deepseek-ai/dsh) plugin architecture.

Personal **WeChat** channel plugin for the [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://npm.im/@deepseek-ai/dsh) — turn `dsh` into a WeChat bot with **one long-lived Agent per chat peer** (true rolling memory, flushed to disk).

This plugin talks **directly** to WeChat's official **iLink Bot API** (the same protocol behind Tencent's `@tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin` gateway plugin). It uses that Tencent-maintained package as a plain protocol library — **no OpenClaw gateway, no forwarding, no cloud relay** — and replaces the gateway glue with DSH Agents:

```
your WeChat ⇄ Tencent iLink API ⇄ this plugin (getUpdates long-poll)
                                        └→ one resident DSH Agent per peer
                                           replies via sendMessage
```

- **QR login** on first boot: the QR link is printed to the log and written to `<rootDir>/login-qr.txt` (render it or open it in WeChat). The flow auto-refreshes expired QRs and retries.
- **Credentials** are stored under `<rootDir>/state/openclaw-weixin/accounts/<bot-id>.json` (0600), isolated from any OpenClaw installation via `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.
- **Inbound**: every text message wakes the peer's Agent (created lazily, memory spans the process lifetime; sessions persist to the DSH session store).
- **Model**: whatever the host's default model selection is (`agent-default-model` in `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`).
- Resilient: long-poll timeouts and transport errors back off exponentially (5s→120s) and reconnect.

readme.section: 1. Put the bundle where DSH resolves bundles, e.g. the runtime install:
2. Install the iLink protocol library into the same runtime:

readme.text:
dsh --profile weixin
```

On first boot it prints a QR link — scan it with your phone WeChat, confirm,
and the bridge enters the poll loop. Subsequent boots reuse the saved token.

```yaml
- id: weixin-bridge
  config:
    rootDir: ~/.dsh/weixin-channel   # state + workspace root
    accountId: default               # logical account label

- **One iLink connection per WeChat account globally** — don't run another
  WeChat gateway (OpenClaw, Hermes, hermesclaw…) on the same account while
  this bridge runs, or tokens will conflict (403s / dropped messages).
- Text messages only in v0.1 (the protocol lib also supports images/voice/
  files — media handling is a natural next step).
- Self-sent messages don't reach the bot channel; test from another account.
- Reply latency = model turn time (tens of seconds typical); the iLink side
  has no typing indicator wired up in v0.1.
